correctness.rationale: Every class is an intersecting family of edges, hence a star subfamily or a triangle. For a proper star of size t≥2, a noncentral edge can see two class edges when t=2, t−1 when t≥3 is odd, and t−2 when t≥4 is even, all positive even counts. A full star gives n−3 neighbors for every noncentral edge and is therefore permitted exactly for even n. Triangles and singletons always work. Two full stars cannot coexist. With P(v) the maximum triangle packing size, the respective costs are C0=binom(n,2)−2P(n) and C*=1+binom(n−1,2)−2P(n−1); equality within a type forces a maximum packing. The verified classical leave sizes give the four formulas and C0−C*=(2n−12)/3, (2n−4)/3, (2n−2)/3 in the even residues 0,2,4, respectively. Independently at n=6, triangles 123,145,246,356 leave a matching; five triples would violate leave-degree parity. In K5, 123 and 145 pack two triples; three would leave one edge, violating even leave degree. These give seven colors in each allowed type and no other optimum type. This verifies all n≥5 and classifies unlabelled color partitions, not named assignments.

value.rationale: This settles a natural infinite subfamily of Kneser graphs for a neighborhood-parity invariant, not just one scalar. The allowable-class lemma and star versus no-star comparison explain how a classical packing problem determines all optimizers, including the exceptional tie; they provide reusable structure beyond the already-known Petersen value.
residual_risks: Does not enumerate maximum packings or imply a higher-rank coloring law.
